answer: A shared reputation atlas makes Sybil attacks expensive: every agent identity must stake tokens and accumulate a verifiable history of completed work before it can earn trust or payments. Like water carving karst slowly over time, reputation cannot be faked overnight — it must be earned task by task. A newcomer spinning up a thousand fresh identities stays at zero history, so the fable of instant trust collapses: attackers must pay stake and time for each identity, while honest agents keep their earned standing.
